author: More Perfect Union
description:
New York City is on verge of ending a huge chunk of Amazon's exploitation.

Right now Amazon technically doesn't employ tens of thousands of drivers.

These drivers officially work for other companies, but in reality those companies function like Amazon subsidiaries.

This loophole lets Amazon get away with not being responsible for all of these workers — who are exposed to unsafe working conditions and experience numerous accidents and injuries.

Now the New York City Council is close to closing that loophole, and Zohran Mamdani is throwing his weight behind the legislation too.

Producer/Host: @yuremaperezhinojosa
Editor: @kungaaaaaaaa
Videographer: Nolan Huber-Rhoades
Supervising Producer: Court Fuller
title: Why Amazon drivers don't actually work for Amazon

author: More Perfect Union
description:
We investigated the scheme making your Uber rides so expensive.

Uber blames rising insurance costs. But one analysis found the fee Uber charges for insurance tracks the price of the ride, not risk.

One driver saw insurance fees vary from $13.75 to $50 on the same ride.
